title: Coherent Control Of Interacting Solid-state Spins Below The Diffraction Limit
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates coherent control of individual rare-earth ion spins below the diffraction limit, enabling addressability of closely spaced spins for quantum networks.
motivation: Solid-state spins are promising for quantum networks but are often too densely packed to be individually addressed, limiting scalability.
method: Uses optical techniques to achieve sub-diffraction-limit addressing and coherent control of interacting rare-earth dopants in a solid-state host.
result: Achieves single-spin control and coherent manipulation of interacting rare-earth spins, overcoming the diffraction barrier.
conclusion: This work enables scalable quantum network nodes using dense ensembles of solid-state spins with individual addressability.

title: A Photonic Integrated Long-distance Quantum Communication Network
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: A photonic integrated quantum network using twin-field QKD over 540 km fiber with full connectivity between four users.
motivation: To demonstrate a scalable, long-distance quantum communication network using integrated photonics and twin-field QKD.
method: A spine-leaf network architecture with four users connected via a central node, using twin-field QKD at 1.25 GHz clock rate over up to 540 km fiber.
result: Achieved a secret key rate of 9.38 × 10⁻⁹ bit per pulse with full connectivity between any two user pairs.
conclusion: The work shows the feasibility of integrated photonic quantum networks for long-distance secure communication.

title: Analytical Computation Of Entanglement Distribution Time In First-generation Quantum Repeater Chains
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Analytical model for entanglement distribution time in first-generation quantum repeater chains.
motivation: Understanding the time required to distribute entanglement over long distances is crucial for designing efficient quantum repeater networks.
method: Derives closed-form expressions for the distribution time considering probabilistic entanglement swapping, memory decoherence, and finite resources.
result: Provides analytical formulas that accurately predict the average entanglement distribution time and its variance for various chain lengths and parameters.
conclusion: The analytical model enables rapid optimization of repeater chain parameters without costly simulations, advancing practical quantum network design.

title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a regret-minimizing online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, achieving near-optimal performance with efficient computational cost.
motivation: Learning unknown quantum states from measurements is fundamental to quantum information processing, but existing methods often suffer from high sample complexity or computational overhead.
method: The authors propose a follow-the-regularized-leader algorithm with a log-determinant barrier, leveraging matrix multiplicative weights and online convex optimization techniques.
result: The algorithm achieves O(√T) regret for pure state tomography, matching the information-theoretic lower bound up to logarithmic factors, and runs in polynomial time per round.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and theoretically optimal approach for online quantum state learning, with implications for adaptive quantum tomography and quantum machine learning.

title: Optimal Control For Rydberg Multi-qubit Operations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents optimal control techniques for multi-qubit operations in Rydberg atom arrays, enhancing gate fidelity and scalability.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multi-qubit gates is challenging due to interactions and decoherence.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to design pulse sequences that minimize gate errors for multi-qubit operations, considering realistic experimental constraints.
result: They demonstrate significant improvements in gate fidelity for two- and three-qubit gates compared to standard methods, with potential for scaling to larger systems.
conclusion: Optimal control provides a practical route to high-fidelity multi-qubit operations in Rydberg platforms, advancing their viability for quantum computing.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With A Leakage From Digital-to-analog Conversion
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper analyzes the security impact of digital-to-analog converter (DAC) leakage in continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) systems.
motivation: Practical CV-QKD systems use DACs to generate modulation signals, but DAC leakage can reveal information to an eavesdropper, compromising security. The authors aim to quantify this leakage and propose countermeasures.
method: The authors model the DAC leakage as an additional side channel and derive the secret key rate under collective attacks using Gaussian optimality. They simulate the effect of leakage on key rate for various system parameters.
result: They find that DAC leakage can significantly reduce the achievable secret key rate, especially at low signal-to-noise ratios, and that the leakage can be mitigated by increasing modulation variance or using post-selection.
conclusion: DAC leakage is a practical security threat in CV-QKD that must be accounted for in system design; the proposed mitigation strategies can restore secure key distribution.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: A context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, but trapped-ion systems often exhibit non-Markovian effects that degrade characterization accuracy.
method: The authors extend gate set tomography to incorporate non-Markovian noise by using a context-aware framework that accounts for temporal correlations in the noise.
result: The method yields more accurate and self-consistent estimates of gate fidelities and error rates compared to standard tomography in the presence of non-Markovian noise.
conclusion: Leveraging non-Markovianity improves the reliability of quantum gate characterization, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing with trapped ions.

title: Design And Optimization Of Adaptive Diversity Schemes In Quantum Mimo Channels
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes and optimizes adaptive diversity schemes for quantum MIMO channels to improve communication reliability and capacity.
motivation: Quantum MIMO channels suffer from fading and noise; adaptive diversity can enhance performance by dynamically selecting transmission strategies.
method: The authors design adaptive diversity protocols that switch between spatial multiplexing and diversity modes based on channel state information, and optimize switching thresholds using convex optimization.
result: The optimized adaptive schemes achieve significant gains in quantum bit error rate and entanglement fidelity compared to fixed schemes.
conclusion: Adaptive diversity is a promising approach for practical quantum MIMO communication systems, balancing throughput and reliability.

title: Long-lived Photon Blockade With Weak Optical Nonlinearity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates long-lived photon blockade using weak optical nonlinearity in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: Photon blockade is a key effect for quantum information processing, but typically requires strong nonlinearities; this work aims to achieve it with weak nonlinearities for practical implementation.
method: The authors propose a scheme using a cavity coupled to a nonlinear medium and exploit interference effects to sustain photon blockade over long times.
result: They show that photon blockade can persist for timescales much longer than the cavity lifetime, even with weak nonlinearity.
conclusion: This approach enables efficient single-photon sources and quantum gates with existing experimental platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ultrashort Light Pulses Can Transform A Semiconductor Into A Topological Insulator
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: Floquet engineering with ultrashort light pulses transiently transforms a semiconductor into a topological insulator by creating light-induced metallic surface states.
motivation: To demonstrate a new method for dynamically inducing topological phases in semiconductors using light, enabling transient topological insulator behavior.
method: The experiment uses ultrashort light pulses to drive a semiconductor, inducing Floquet-Bloch bands and creating metallic surface states within the band gap.
result: Light-induced surface states are observed, transiently turning the semiconductor into a topological insulator.
conclusion: Floquet engineering can dynamically create topological phases in semiconductors, offering a route to optically controlled topological materials.

title: Hidden Loop Currents In A Kagome Metal
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: Nuclear quadrupole resonance and NMR reveal tiny internal magnetic fields in a kagome metal, indicating hidden loop currents consistent with an imaginary charge-density wave.
motivation: To find microscopic evidence of hidden electronic order in kagome metals, specifically spontaneous atomic-scale current loops.
method: Nuclear quadrupole resonance and nuclear magnetic resonance measurements to detect tiny internal magnetic fields.
result: Observation of tiny internal magnetic fields providing microscopic evidence of hidden loop currents.
conclusion: The observed fields are consistent with an imaginary charge-density wave, revealing a new type of electronic order.

title: Angular Momentum Of Rotating Fermionic Superfluids By Sagnac Phonon Interferometry
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper measures the angular momentum per particle in rotating fermionic superfluids across the BEC-BCS crossover using a Sagnac phonon interferometer.
motivation: To directly link fermionic pairing to macroscopic superflow and measure the quantum of angular momentum per particle.
method: A Sagnac-like phonon interferometer is used to probe the angular momentum of rotating fermionic superfluids.
result: Measurements of angular momentum per particle are achieved across the BEC-BCS crossover.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates a new way to probe superfluid properties in fermionic systems.

title: Anomalous Crossover From Three-dimensional Heisenberg To Two-dimensional Ising Magnetism In A Van Der Waals Magnet
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports an anomalous crossover from 3D Heisenberg to 2D Ising magnetism in a van der Waals magnet via self-intercalation.
motivation: Understanding how dimensionality and anisotropy affect magnetic order in low-dimensional systems is a fundamental question in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use self-intercalation in Fe3GeTe2 to tune the magnetic interactions and characterize the magnetic ordering using experimental techniques.
result: They observe a crossover from three-dimensional Heisenberg to two-dimensional Ising ferromagnetism as a function of self-intercalation.
conclusion: Self-intercalation provides a new way to control magnetic dimensionality and anisotropy in van der Waals magnets.

title: Floquet Topological State Induced By Light-driven Band Inversion In SnTe
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: Femtosecond light pulses induce a transient topological state in SnTe via band inversion.
motivation: To demonstrate light-driven topological phase transitions in a semiconductor, which has been theoretically predicted but lacked clear experimental evidence.
method: Femtosecond laser pulses are used to drive band inversion in SnTe, and the resulting topological state is probed via time-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
result: A transient topological state is observed in SnTe under light irradiation, which is absent at equilibrium.
conclusion: Light can be used to engineer topological phases in semiconductors on ultrafast timescales.

title: How To Probe Lattice Dynamics Using Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a technique for probing lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy.
motivation: To provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.
method: Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy is used to measure phonon modes.
result: The technique enables detailed characterization of lattice dynamics.
conclusion: Brillouin spectroscopy is a powerful tool for studying lattice dynamics.

title: Fullqubit Alchemist: Quantum Algorithm For Alchemical Free Energy Calculations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm for alchemical free energy calculations, a method used in computational chemistry to compute free energy differences between molecular systems.
motivation: Alchemical free energy calculations are important for drug discovery and materials science but are computationally expensive on classical computers; quantum algorithms may offer speedups.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that uses Hamiltonian simulation and phase estimation to compute free energy differences via alchemical transformations, leveraging the quantum computer's ability to simulate quantum systems.
result: The algorithm is analyzed theoretically and demonstrated on small molecules, showing potential for polynomial speedup over classical methods, though practical implementation remains challenging.
conclusion: Quantum algorithms for alchemical free energy calculations are feasible in principle but require fault-tolerant quantum computers with many logical qubits to outperform classical methods.

title: Data-driven Discovery Of Dynamical Models In Biology
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026;
tldr: A technical review of data-driven methods for discovering dynamical models in biology.
motivation: To compare regression-based, network-based, and decomposition techniques for extracting dynamical information from time-resolved biological data.
method: Review and comparative analysis of various data-driven approaches including regression, neural networks, and decomposition methods.
result: Identifies strengths, limitations, and complementarity of different approaches for biological dynamical modeling.
conclusion: Data-driven methods are powerful for biological dynamics but require careful selection based on data characteristics and problem context.

title: Radioactive Molecules As Laboratories Of Fundamental Physics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This perspective article discusses using radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei for precision tests of fundamental physics, such as symmetry violations and new physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To explore the potential of radioactive molecules as a platform for fundamental physics measurements complementary to high-energy colliders.
method: Review of advances in production, trapping, and quantum control of radioactive molecules, focusing on octupole-deformed nuclei.
result: Identifies that these molecules offer enhanced sensitivity to symmetry-violating effects due to their nuclear structure.
conclusion: Radioactive molecules are a promising laboratory for probing new physics, but the paper is a perspective without new experimental or theoretical results.

title: Electrospray Ion Beam Deposition For Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy Of Complex Molecules
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a method for depositing complex molecules onto surfaces for scanning tunnelling microscopy, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Imaging complex molecules on surfaces is important for molecular electronics and nanotechnology, but the paper does not connect to quantum information processing or thermodynamics.
method: Electrospray ion beam deposition is used to deposit intact complex molecules onto a substrate for STM imaging.
result: The method enables surface imaging of complex molecules that are difficult to deposit by other means.
conclusion: The technique advances molecular surface science but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: The Costs And Benefits Of Physics Research
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the environmental costs and benefits of physics research, advocating for cost-benefit analysis that includes environmental impacts.
motivation: To highlight the environmental footprint of physics research and encourage sustainable practices.
method: Commentary and perspective piece, likely reviewing existing literature and proposing a framework.
result: Argues that environmental impacts should be considered in decisions about what physics research to pursue.
conclusion: Physics research should incorporate environmental cost-benefit analysis to reduce its ecological footprint.

title: Atomic Force Microscopy From Nanoscale Imaging To Holistic Exploration
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: A commentary on the evolution of atomic force microscopy from imaging to a versatile nanoscience platform.
motivation: To highlight the broad impact and versatility of atomic force microscopy beyond surface imaging.
method: Historical and technical commentary tracing key innovations in AFM.
result: AFM has become a multipurpose tool for nanoscale characterization.
conclusion: AFM continues to expand its role in nanoscience and beyond.

title: Enhancing Molecular Property Prediction Of Transformer Models With Dual Graph Representation
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a dual graph transformer model that integrates atom, bond, topology, structure, and stereogeometric features via self-attention to improve molecular property prediction.
motivation: Accurate molecular property prediction is crucial for drug discovery and materials science, but existing models often fail to capture complex molecular features like stereochemistry.
method: The authors propose a dual graph transformer architecture that fuses multiple molecular representations (atom, bond, topology, structure, stereogeometry) within a self-attention mechanism.
result: The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on several molecular property prediction benchmarks, demonstrating the benefit of incorporating diverse graph features.
conclusion: Dual graph representation with self-attention effectively enhances molecular property prediction, offering a promising approach for computational chemistry.

title: Highly Robust Molecular Information Carriers For Traceability Of Plastic Materials
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a molecular tagging strategy using sequence-defined oligoamides for traceability of plastic materials.
motivation: To enable traceability of plastic materials through molecular information carriers that can withstand industrial processing conditions.
method: The authors incorporate abiotic sequence-defined oligoamides at ultralow concentrations into polymers and test their resilience under thermal and chemical conditions typical of industrial polymer processing.
result: The oligoamide tags endure the harsh processing conditions and can be read out, providing a robust molecular barcode for plastic traceability.
conclusion: This molecular tagging approach offers a practical solution for tracing plastic materials throughout their lifecycle, with potential applications in recycling and quality control.

title: A Minimal In Vitro Assay For Cell Intercalation Highlights The Importance Of Interfacial Tension And Migratory Forces
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies cell intercalation in a minimal in vitro system, focusing on mechanical forces like interfacial tension and migratory forces.
motivation: Understanding the physical mechanisms driving cell intercalation, a key process in morphogenesis.
method: A minimal assay with four cells is used to measure and model the roles of junction tension and migratory forces.
result: Intercalation is driven by both interfacial tension and migratory forces, with quantitative agreement between experiments and simulations.
conclusion: The minimal system captures essential physics of cell intercalation, highlighting the importance of mechanical forces.

title: The Relative Effectiveness Of Active Learning Methods
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: A multi-institutional study comparing the effectiveness of four active learning methods in introductory physics classrooms.
motivation: To determine which active learning methods are most effective in physics education, as their comparative effectiveness is unclear.
method: Multi-institutional study comparing four well-established active learning methods in introductory physics courses.
result: The study provides comparative data on the effectiveness of the four methods.
conclusion: The findings help educators choose the most effective active learning strategies for physics instruction.

title: Spatiotemporal Shaping Of Broadband Helical Light Pulses At Relativistic Intensities
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates the generation of helical light pulses with orbital angular momentum at relativistic intensities, a topic in high-intensity laser physics.
motivation: To achieve controlled spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum in high-power laser systems for applications in laser-plasma interactions.
method: Experimental setup using a large-scale laser facility to generate and characterize broadband helical light pulses at relativistic intensities.
result: Peak intensities above 1.4 × 10^18 W cm−2 were achieved with controlled spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum.
conclusion: The technique enables new regimes of light-matter interaction at relativistic intensities with structured light.

title: Self-organized Nanoplasmonic Artificial Leaf For Hot-carrier Bioelectronic Interfaces
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a self-organized nanoplasmonic artificial leaf device for hot-carrier bioelectronic interfaces, enabling leadless optoelectronic modulation and pattern recognition.
motivation: To develop a bioelectronic interface that can efficiently convert light into electrical signals for modulating biological systems without physical leads.
method: The authors fabricate a nanoplasmonic artificial leaf using self-organized nanostructures that generate hot carriers upon light absorption, and characterize its optoelectronic performance.
result: The device exhibits linear performance over a wide range of light intensities and enables leadless multimodal optoelectronic modulation and pixel-less optical pattern recognition.
conclusion: The self-organized nanoplasmonic artificial leaf offers a promising platform for bioelectronic interfaces and optical computing applications.

title: Deuterated Compounds For Organic Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: A review of deuterated compounds for organic light-emitting diodes, focusing on deuteration advantages and mechanisms.
motivation: To survey recent advances in deuterated compounds for improving OLED performance and stability.
method: Review of literature on deuteration effects in organic semiconductors and device applications.
result: Deuteration can enhance device efficiency and lifetime by reducing non-radiative decay and improving stability.
conclusion: Deuterated compounds offer promising routes for next-generation OLEDs, but wider implementation requires further research.

title: Overcoming The Fill-factor Limit Of Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: This paper addresses the fill-factor limit in organic solar cells through a guest-host design that prolongs exciton lifetime, improving both fill factor and open-circuit voltage.
motivation: Organic solar cells suffer from fill-factor limitations due to field-dependent charge generation caused by exciton/charge-transfer coupling, which hinders efficiency.
method: The authors combine modeling with a novel guest-host material design to extend exciton lifetime, thereby reducing field-dependent losses.
result: The proposed design simultaneously increases the fill factor and open-circuit voltage, overcoming the traditional fill-factor limit.
conclusion: The guest-host approach offers a pathway to higher efficiency organic solar cells by addressing the exciton/charge-transfer coupling issue.

title: Super-Snell Scanning Light-field Display For Ultrawide-angle High-resolution Glasses-free Three-dimensional Displays
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A scanning light-field display achieving ultrawide-angle, high-resolution glasses-free 3D display using Snell's window effect.
motivation: To overcome the trade-off between viewing angle and resolution in glasses-free 3D displays.
method: A scanning light-field architecture inspired by Snell's window effect in nature.
result: Demonstrated a 150° viewing angle with nearly 480-pixel resolution.
conclusion: The proposed architecture enables practical ultrawide-angle high-resolution 3D displays.

title: Author Correction: Single-shot Terahertz-field-driven X-ray Streak Camera
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This is an author correction for a paper on a terahertz-field-driven X-ray streak camera, which is an ultrafast measurement technique.
motivation: The original paper presented a method for single-shot X-ray streak cameras using terahertz fields for ultrafast time-resolved measurements.
method: The correction likely addresses errors or updates in the original publication.
result: No new scientific results; it is a correction notice.
conclusion: The paper is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Wide-temperature-range Fluid-phase Grain Boundaries For Temperature-robust Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method to improve perovskite solar cell efficiency and stability using fluid-phase grain boundaries.
motivation: Perovskite solar cells suffer from thermal cycling instability due to grain boundary defects; the authors aim to enhance durability and efficiency.
method: They introduce a wide-temperature-range fluid-phase molecular complex that forms dynamically adaptive grain boundaries in perovskite films.
result: The approach achieves an efficiency of 26.52% and improved thermal cycling stability.
conclusion: Fluid-phase grain boundaries offer a promising route to temperature-robust perovskite solar cells.

title: Forty Years Of Atomic Force Microscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A viewpoint article celebrating 40 years of atomic force microscopy, discussing its diverse applications and future developments.
motivation: To reflect on the impact and evolution of AFM as a key experimental technique across physics and other sciences.
method: Seven scientists provide their perspectives on how they use AFM and their hopes for its future.
result: The article presents a collection of viewpoints rather than new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: AFM remains a versatile and essential tool, with ongoing developments expected to expand its capabilities.

title: The Physics Of GaN-based Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A review of the physics of GaN-based LEDs, focusing on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects.
motivation: GaN-based LEDs are crucial for modern lighting, but their efficiency is governed by complex physical effects that need to be understood.
method: The review synthesizes existing research on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects in GaN LEDs.
result: The paper describes how these three effects impact LED performance, including efficiency droop and emission wavelength.
conclusion: Understanding these physical mechanisms is key to further improving GaN LED efficiency and light output.

title: Wild Tomato Genome Assemblies Reveal Structural Variants And Repeat Content Act As Recombination Barriers
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 28 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents genome assemblies of wild tomato species and analyzes structural variants and repeat content as barriers to meiotic recombination.
motivation: To understand how structural variation and repetitive elements influence recombination in wild tomatoes, which could inform breeding strategies for modern tomatoes.
method: The authors sequenced and assembled genomes of multiple wild tomato species, then performed comparative genomics to identify structural variants and repeat content, correlating them with recombination patterns.
result: Structural variants and repeat content were found to act as barriers to meiotic recombination, affecting the distribution of crossovers.
conclusion: These findings provide insights into the genomic factors that shape recombination landscapes in tomatoes, with implications for crop improvement.

title: Hyperbranched Dielectric Polymer Networks Exhibiting Giant Energy Storage Density At 250 °c
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents hyperbranched dielectric polymer networks that achieve high energy storage density at high temperature.
motivation: To overcome charge transfer and achieve efficient capacitive energy storage in dielectric polymers at thermal extremes up to 250°C.
method: Design hyperbranched networks to expand inter-chain spacing and suppress secondary relaxation.
result: Achieved 4.9 J/cm³ energy density with 90% efficiency at 250°C.
conclusion: Hyperbranched network design is effective for high-temperature capacitive energy storage.

title: Prediction Error Correlates In The Striosome-dopamine Circuit Emerge From Information Gain
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes that dopamine signals in the brain track information gain about action selection, unifying learning, movement, and decision-making.
motivation: To explain how dopamine and striosome circuits coordinate diverse functions like learning, movement, and decision-making under a single principle.
method: The authors develop a computational model where dopamine encodes the information gain from new information about which action to take, and test it against neural data.
result: Dopamine signals correlate with prediction error defined as information gain, not reward prediction error, unifying its roles.
conclusion: Dopamine's diverse functions can be understood as tracking information gain, providing a unified framework for striosome-dopamine circuit function.

title: Nad+ Modulates Mitochondrial Vulnerability In MERTK-associated Models Of Retinitis Pigmentosa
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the role of NAD+ in mitochondrial vulnerability in MERTK-associated retinitis pigmentosa, a retinal degenerative disease.
motivation: Retinitis pigmentosa leads to blindness due to photoreceptor loss, and understanding mitochondrial mechanisms may reveal therapeutic targets.
method: The authors use MERTK-associated models of retinitis pigmentosa and administer the NAD+ precursor NMN to assess effects on retinal degeneration and mitochondrial function.
result: NMN protects against retinal degeneration by improving mitochondrial function in these models.
conclusion: NAD+ modulation offers potential therapeutic insights for treating retinitis pigmentosa.

title: Ecological Multifunctionality Of Watersheds Increases With Tree Species Richness
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the relationship between tree species richness and watershed multifunctionality, finding a positive but climate-dependent effect.
motivation: Understanding how biodiversity shapes ecosystem functions across large landscapes is crucial for conservation and management.
method: The authors analyzed forest tree diversity and watershed multifunctionality data across a large geographic scale, using statistical models to assess the effect of species richness and its interaction with aridity.
result: Higher tree species richness increases watershed multifunctionality, but the effect weakens in arid climates.
conclusion: Biodiversity conservation can enhance ecosystem multifunctionality, but its benefits are context-dependent, particularly under water-limited conditions.

title: Multiple Human Transgenes Prolong Survival Of Triple-carbohydrate Knockout Porcine Kidney Xenografts In Nonhuman Primates
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies genetically modified pig kidney xenografts in nonhuman primates, focusing on immune rejection and graft survival.
motivation: To improve xenotransplantation outcomes by reducing immune rejection through genetic modifications.
method: Triple-carbohydrate knockout pigs were further engineered with human transgenes (TNFAIP3, HMOX1) and kidney grafts were transplanted into nonhuman primates.
result: Adding human transgenes dampened immune responses and prolonged graft survival.
conclusion: Genetic modifications including human transgenes can improve the viability of porcine xenografts.
